analysis.title: Nowhere To Hide: Stock Pickers And Quants Both Lose 3%+ In October For The First Time On Goldman's Record
key_insights: Goldman Prime Brokerage reports global Fundamental L/S funds lost 3.49% and Systematic L/S funds lost 3.6% in October 2026. It is the first month on record (since 2016) in which both cohorts fell 3% or more, while MSCI World fell 0.77% and the S&P 500 fell 0.87%.
TMT-focused funds lost 12.6% in October and are up 5.1% YTD, so about three-quarters of their 2026 gains were erased in one month. Asia L/S managers lost 9.4% and remain up 14% YTD.

Ex-beta, global Fundamental L/S alpha was -1.75%, the worst since July and second worst in more than four years. Biggest detractors were Volatility, China, Short-Term Momentum and Short Crowdedness. Gains came from the US, Health Care and Size.

Systematic L/S returned -3.6%, the first down month since Jul '25 and the worst drawdown in six years, driven entirely by negative long side alpha. Beta added 1.47%, so systematic alpha was -5.06%. YTD Systematic L/S total return is +16.2%.
Goldman's momentum basket swung from +27% in September to -18.6% in October.

Asset-weighted Fundamental L/S return (-3.49%) was worse than the equal-weighted average (-0.98%) and the median (-1.69%), which Goldman reads as large managers underperforming. Top-to-bottom quartile dispersion was 10.4 points, with the 25th percentile fund at -7.97%.

The median Fundamental L/S fund is up 1.16% YTD against 10.89% for MSCI World and 11.77% for the S&P 500. The bottom quartile is down 9.88% YTD. Morgan Stanley's Nick Savone says about 35-40% of L/S funds are flat or negative YTD and hedge funds are underweight the broader AI trade for the first time since early 2023.

The global book saw its largest dollar net selling since March, split evenly between long and short sales. Single stocks were net sold with long sales outpacing short sales 4 to 1. Macro products (index and ETFs) were net bought, with long buys outpacing short sales 1.6 to 1.

Overall prime book net leverage fell 4.2 points to 73.4%, the fastest drop since March. Gross leverage rose 4.8 points to 314.5% (97th percentile on five years), driven by mark-to-market according to Goldman.

Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.2 points to 49.2% (3rd percentile on one year). Gross rose 4.2 points to 210.7%. The long/short ratio fell 4.3% to 1.610, the 1st percentile on five years. Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 21.6 points to 40.9%.

North America was net sold for a second straight month with short sales outpacing long buys 3.5 to 1. Hedge funds are 15.2% underweight North America versus MSCI ACWI (8th percentile on five years). EM Asia had the largest net selling since July, with Taiwan, Korea and China all net sold. The KOSPI drawdown since late September reached about 16-17% per Morgan Stanley.

Info Tech saw the largest net selling since June with long sales outpacing short sales 4.5 to 1. Every subsector was sold except Software. Materials saw the largest net selling since May 2024, with a long/short ratio of 1.77 (1st percentile). Defensives were net bought for the first time in seven months, mostly through short covers.
Consumer staples had their best month since October 2000.

Bull case: positioning is about as bearish as in five years. Goldman's Prime desk read the October stop-outs as a buy-the-dip setup. Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson says the mid-cycle correction is entering its final stages. Funds this underweight AI and net short have historically produced squeezes.

Bear case: Savone warns of the 'final drop of the log flume' with hyperscalers still facing a potential washout. Wilson expects semis to find support around mid-November, potentially after another 10-15% decline. Goldman's Sharkey flags the Mag7, the most crowded AI cohort, as the next source of funds. Goldman's Coppersmith warns discretionary selling may give way to systematic selling, with CTAs sitting on a $65 billion trapdoor under the S&P.

Retail flows per Morgan Stanley QDS turned negative on Monday. Goldman's IG 100 index broke through its 2026 wides, and Oracle is reported to be nearing a $10 billion share sale at an 11% discount. The author expects the bearish path to be more likely, with the midterms on Tuesday and the AI financing debate as catalysts.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is about as bearish as in five years. Goldman's Prime desk read the October stop-outs as a buy-the-dip setup, Morgan Stanley's Wilson says the mid-cycle correction is entering its final stages, and funds this underweight AI and net short have historically produced squeezes. The median fund is up only 1%, leaving room to chase if the tape turns.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage is in the 97th percentile while net is in the 9th, so de-grossing is unfinished. Mag7 is the next source of funds, hyperscalers face a potential washout per Savone, Wilson sees semis possibly falling another 10-15%, CTAs have a $65 billion trapdoor under the S&P, and retail flows turned negative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gross leverage falling meaningfully from the 97th percentile would signal de-grossing is complete. The author also points to Tuesday's midterms and the AI financing debate as the catalysts.

theme_stances.key_argument: The de-grossing that started in October is not finished until gross itself comes down, and that probably means Mag7 is the next shoe to drop.
